title: Ball 2's initial speed
description: Essential: The response must correctly calculate the initial horizontal speed of ball 2 (4 m/s) from its projectile motion data.

title: Ball 1's initial speed
description: Essential: The response must correctly apply momentum conservation to find the initial speed of ball 1 (10 m/s) after the spring releases.

title: Elastic potential energy
description: Essential: The final answer for part (1) must be the correct elastic potential energy (14 J), calculated from the kinetic energies of both balls.

title: Speed at highest point
description: Important: The response must correctly apply energy conservation (work-energy theorem) to find the speed of ball 1 at the top of the circular track.

title: Net force at point A
description: Important: The response must correctly apply Newton's second law for circular motion at the top of the track to find the normal force from the track.

title: Pressure on the track
description: Essential: The final answer for part (2) must be the correct magnitude of the pressure (10 N), found via Newton's third law from the calculated normal force.

title: Projectile time error
description: Pitfall: Incorrectly calculating the time of flight for ball 2 (e.g., using horizontal distance only) should be penalized.

title: Sign/direction error at top
description: Pitfall: Incorrectly applying the sign for forces at the top of the loop (e.g., adding centripetal force instead of net force) should be penalized.

title: Unit consistency
description: Optional: The response demonstrates consistent use of SI units (m, s, J, N) throughout the calculation.
